newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firms seen buying more U.S. corn.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firms seen buying more U.S. corn.

text.p: Philippine feed millers and livestock farmers plan to import more U.S. corn because of a supply shortage that is lifting domestic prices, industry officials and traders said on Tuesday.
"Prices are firming up and we cannot wait for help from the National Food Authority (NFA)," said Edward Acosta, vice president for the feeds division at Swift Foods Inc.

On Monday, feed millers and swine farmers bought 55,000 tonnes of number 2 U.S. yellow corn at $137.75 per tonne C&F. Continental Grains Co won the tender to supply the corn for July 10-25 arrival, traders said.
At $137.75 per tonne, the equivalent landed cost in Manila of the U.S. corn was 7.15 pesos per kg against the prevailing domestic wholesale price of eight pesos per kg, Acosta said.
Traders said the landed cost of the corn could have been lower at 5.12 pesos per kg if it was imported by the NFA.
NFA corn importations are slapped with a 35 percent tariff against 80 percent for the private sector.
Traders said they expected domestic prices to increase as the main Philippine corn harvest was not due to start until July.
"It's so hard to buy corn these days. The February to May harvests in Ilocos and Cagayan Valley regions are over," Acosta said.
"Expect more importations from the private sector even at 80 percent tariff if domestic prices remain firmer compared to imports," a senior trader said.
Feed millers and hog raisers have asked the state-owned NFA in the past weeks to import an additional 300,000 tonnes of corn before July this year due to a shortage.
The importation must obtain the approval of President Fidel Ramos and the Congress.
The NFA has so far imported 120,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China and 25,000 tonnes of U.S. white corn since the start of the year.
Acosta said industrial corn users in the Philippines preferred U.S. corn because of its better quality.
Private firms have estimated the domestic corn shortage this year at one to two million tonnes.
